# How to Set Up a Shared Grocery List in Alexa That Anyone Can Add to by Voice

> **In short:** You don't need a special setting. Alexa already keeps a shopping list, and Amazon says Alexa lets everyone in the household add in-the-moment needs to it — anyone at home can say "Alexa, add eggs to my shopping list" to your Echo. To let a second adult see the same list on their own account, add them to your Amazon Family on amazon.com; Amazon says all adults in an Amazon Family share Amazon Shopping Lists.

The grocery list fails at the worst moment: someone used the last of the milk, nobody wrote it down, and you find out in the store. With Alexa, the list fills itself up — whoever notices says one sentence to the nearest Echo, and the item is waiting for you when you shop.

## Before you start
- **At least one Echo device** set up with your Amazon account, somewhere the family passes every day — the kitchen is ideal.
- **The Alexa app** on your phone, signed in with the same Amazon account.
- **Optional, for a second adult:** their own Amazon account. Amazon Family has room for up to 2 adults, each with their own Amazon account, plus teen and child profiles.
- **Time needed:** about 5 minutes, plus a few minutes if you invite a second adult.

## Step 1 — Open the shopping list Alexa already keeps
Open the **Alexa app**, tap **More**, then **Lists & Notes**, and open your shopping list. This is the list Alexa uses when someone asks to add something to "my shopping list". Amazon says it is available on your Echo devices, in the Alexa app, and in the Amazon app — so you can check it at home, online, or in the store.

**If it looks different:** if you've never used lists before, the shopping list may be empty. That's fine — the next step puts the first item on it.

**You'll know it worked when** your shopping list is open in the Alexa app.

## Step 2 — Add the first item by voice
Walk to your Echo and add something you actually need. Amazon's own example is the simplest sentence to teach the family.

💬 Example: say *"Alexa, add eggs to my shopping list."*

**If it looks different:** if the item doesn't show up, check your other lists under **Lists & Notes** — if Alexa heard a different list name, the item may be there instead.

**You'll know it worked when** the item appears on your shopping list in the Alexa app.

## Step 3 — Let everyone at home add items the same way
This is where the list becomes shared. Amazon describes the shopping list as a way for everyone in the household to capture needs the moment they come up. Anyone who speaks to your Echo — a partner, a teenager, a roommate — adds to the same list, with no app and no extra setup.

💬 Example: your teenager says *"Alexa, add cereal to my shopping list."* For something added by mistake, Amazon's pattern is "Remove [item] from my [list name]": *"Alexa, remove cereal from my shopping list."*

**You'll know it worked when** an item someone else said out loud appears on the list in your app.

## Step 4 — Share the list with a second adult through Amazon Family
If another adult wants the list on their own phone, with their own account, add them to your Amazon Family. Amazon Family is not managed in the Alexa app — you set it up on the Amazon website. Go to the **Amazon Family** page on amazon.com, under **New — Add a new member** select **Send an Invite**, enter their name and email address, then select **Continue**. Amazon says the invitation stays valid for 14 days.

Once they accept, Amazon says all the adults in your Amazon Family share Amazon Shopping Lists.

**If it looks different:** if your Amazon Family already has two adults, it's full. Everyone can still add to the list by talking to your Echo, and Amazon's grocery help says you can also share the list with others by text message or email.

**You'll know it worked when** the other adult accepts the invitation and can open the shopping list on their own account.

## Step 5 — Check the list before you shop
Before you leave, ask Alexa to read it, or open it on your phone in the store.

💬 Example: say *"Alexa, what's on my shopping list?"* — Amazon's list page says Alexa reads aloud the first five items. For the full list, open it in the Alexa app or the Amazon app.

**You'll know it worked when** you can see or hear everything the family added, without anyone texting you a reminder.

## Common mistakes
- **Looking for a "household" switch in the Alexa app.** There isn't one to find there: Amazon says Amazon Family isn't managed in the Alexa app.
  - **Fix:** everyone at home can already add through your Echo; to add a second adult's account, use the Amazon Family page on amazon.com (Step 4).
- **Saying a different list name.** "Add milk to groceries" can send the item to another list if you have one with a similar name.
  - **Fix:** teach one sentence and stick to it: "Alexa, add [item] to my shopping list."
- **Inviting a third adult.** Amazon Family has room for up to 2 adults.
  - **Fix:** other people at home can still add by voice, and you can share the list by text message or email.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** the list builds itself during the week. Whoever opens the last box of cereal says one sentence, and it's on the list before they forget.
- **For your business or work:** the same habit works for a small office or shared workspace — one Echo near the coffee machine, one sentence for "we're out of filters".
- **If you're just getting started:** begin with voice only for a week. Add the Amazon Family invitation later, once you know the family actually uses the list.

## Try it now
Open the Alexa app, tap **More → Lists & Notes**, and open your shopping list. Then walk to your Echo and say: *"Alexa, add [something you need] to my shopping list."* Check your phone — when the item is there, the family's list is ready.
